subject: Hosting impact scoring and migration handoff
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@datacraft.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting impact scoring and migration handoff

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the team internally and give you a clean decision path.

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost and latencies for your real-time summarization endpoint (SLO: <150ms p95).
- Current topology: mixed setup — AtlasAI hosted endpoints for new traffic, plus an on-prem GPU pool (K8s + proprietary scheduler) for legacy batch scoring.
- Constraints: SOC2 evidence required, strict VPC peering policy with no public egress for certain records, and a Q3 timeline for cutover of the real-time path.

Hosting modes we discussed (impact bullets):
1) Hosted API (Redwood) — fastest to production, lowest ops, can meet latency with our verified models; downside: additional compliance gating for your private data flows.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and private storage of keys/metrics; good middle ground for cost predictability and network isolation (recommended if you need steady throughput >300 rps).
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full control and compliance; longer lead time (network setup + KMS integration), best for customers with strict egress/no-public-internet rules.

Immediate asks / decision points we need from you so we can size the runway:
- Which traffic needs to be in the private-only bucket (PII vs non-PII)? a short list will do.
- Expected steady-state qps and expected peak qps for the real-time endpoint.
- Whether you can provision a CIDR range for peering if we proceed with Private VPC.

Suggested next steps (my recommendation):
- You: share a 1-pager with traffic split and qps estimates.
- Us: run a short impact scoring exercise (latency/cost delta) for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and deliver a one-page scorecard.
- If Dedicated looks promising, we’ll produce a 30-day reserved-capacity POC plan and a sizing estimate (attached: draft estimate).

Attachments: redwood_migration_checklist.xlsx (initial checklist), dedicated-sizing-estimate.pdf (draft).

Availability: I can schedule a 30-minute follow-up on Monday afternoon to walk the scorecard.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Elena Morozova <elena@datacraft.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <raj@platforms.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting impact scoring and migration handoff

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side so the scorecard is accurate: 

1) Traffic split: roughly 70% non-PII (customer-facing summarization), 30% PII (internal compliance summaries). The PII flows cannot leave our VPC.
2) QPS: steady 120 rps for the real-time endpoint; expected peaks ~420 rps during batch windows.
3) CIDR: we can provision /20 for peering but need to run this by infra (I’ll confirm).

Other asks:
- Can you confirm whether the Dedicated option supports persistent KV cache across warm restarts? That’s a blocker for our latency profile.
- What telemetry can we expect for per-token cost breakdown (we want token-level billing by route for finance).

Happy to confirm the 1-pager by EOD tomorrow. Also looping Raj on the infra/cost questions.

—Elena
Elena Morozova
Head of ML Platforms, DataCraft
elena@datacraft.ai

> Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the team internally and give you a clean decision path.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@datacraft.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting impact scoring and migration handoff

Elena — great, that QPS split is exactly what we need. Quick answers to your blockers and a proposed POC path: 

1) Dedicated & KV cache: yes — our Dedicated runtime supports persistent KV caching across instance restarts within a pool (we persist hot segments to local NVMe and replicate metadata). For strict warm-start persistence across full cluster restarts we recommend Private with a mounted NFS/KV backing, but Dedicated covers most real-time SLOs.
2) Token-level billing: Redwood Console exposes token-level usage per route and model, and we can add a billing export to your S3 bucket on a daily cadence (CSV).

Proposed POC (two tracked phases):
- Phase A (7–14 days): Hosted API quick proof to validate model/latency characteristics on representative traffic (non-PII).
- Phase B (30 days): Dedicated capacity POC with a reserved pool + network policy tests for integration. During Phase B we’ll:
  - run traffic replay from your staging traces,
  - validate p95 latency under steady/peak loads,
  - enable the token-level billing export to your S3.

If the PII flows must be private-only, we’ll run a parallel Private VPC scoping exercise (network/pen-test schedule + KMS integration) but that will add ~4–6 weeks.

Next steps: if you confirm the CIDR availability, I’ll route this to our infra team to start the VPC worksheet and lock in a tentative start date for Phase B.

I’ve attached the checklist with the fields we need filled; Marissa will help schedule the follow-up.

Best — Priya

[attachment: redwood_migration_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Elena Morozova <elena@datacraft.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting impact scoring and migration handoff

Elena / Priya — quick note from infra perspective:

- Dedicated sizing: given the 120 steady / 420 peak numbers, initial conservative sizing is a 6-GPU reserved pool (A100-class equiv) with autoscale headroom for 8 GPUs. I attached a short PDF with the estimate and cost parity numbers vs Hosted.
- KV persistence: to clarify Priya’s note, Dedicated persists to local NVMe within the pool; if you need cluster-level persistent KV across full pool reprovisioning, Private with a managed NFS/KV is required.
- Migration from your legacy GPU cluster: we can import model artifacts and checkpoint formats, but we’ll need a small adapter for your scheduler. We’ve done that adapter pattern with two customers; it’s ~2–3 engineer-weeks for the adapter + a replay-based validation.

If you can confirm a PO window, we can commit to the 30-day Dedicated POC start within 2 weeks of contract signature.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks all — this is helpful. Quick confirmations:
- CIDR: infra approved /20, I’ll send the ticket with the exact block later today.
- We will proceed with Phase A (Hosted quick proof) for non-PII immediately after we sign the NDA; DataCraft legal will ping you on the document.
- For Phase B, we prefer Dedicated for cost predictability and to avoid a full Private lift right away. We’ll expect the adapter work for our scheduler (I’ll share build docs).

Planned next steps from our side:
- EOD today: send CIDR and the 1-pager with traffic split + representative traces (S3 link).
- Early next week: legal to circulate NDA; Raj will coordinate infra ticketing.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Elena
